en.short: You are standing in front of Basel's Town Hall, the bright red building on Marktplatz. It was built in the early sixteenth century, shortly after Basel joined the Swiss Confederation in 1501, and it still houses the cantonal government and parliament today.
en.long: Look up at the painted facade: the colourful frescoes and the gilded clock were added and restored over several centuries, and the building was extended around 1900 with the tall tower on the left. Step through the main archway into the courtyard if it is open. The staircase walls are covered with murals, and you will find a statue of Munatius Plancus, the Roman general traditionally credited with founding the nearby colony of Augusta Raurica. Marktplatz itself has hosted a market for centuries, and on most weekday mornings you can still buy fruit, flowers and cheese here.

es.short: Estás frente al Ayuntamiento de Basilea, el edificio rojo de la Marktplatz. Se construyó a principios del siglo XVI, poco después de que Basilea se uniera a la Confederación Suiza en 1501, y todavía acoge el gobierno y el parlamento del cantón.

en.short: This slender Gothic fountain on Fischmarkt dates back to around 1390, making it one of the most important late-medieval fountains in Switzerland. As the name suggests, fish was once sold on this square.
en.long: The figures on the column show the Virgin Mary, Saint Peter and John the Baptist, surrounded by prophets and angels. What you see today is a copy: the fragile original sculptures are kept safe in the Historical Museum. For centuries, fountains like this one were the city's water supply, and Basel still has more than two hundred public fountains. The water is drinkable, so feel free to refill your bottle.

es.short: Esta esbelta fuente gótica de la plaza Fischmarkt data de alrededor de 1390 y es una de las fuentes medievales más importantes de Suiza. Como indica su nombre, aquí se vendía pescado.

en.short: This is the Middle Bridge, on the site of one of the oldest crossings of the Rhine, first built in the 1220s. It connects Grossbasel, the old town on the hill, with Kleinbasel on the other bank.
en.long: The stone bridge you are walking on was completed in 1905, replacing a medieval structure that was partly made of wood. Look for the small chapel in the middle, called the Käppelijoch. In the Middle Ages, it marked a grim spot: convicted criminals were sometimes thrown into the river from here. Today couples hang love locks on its grille. On the Kleinbasel side, find the Lällekönig, a crowned head that sticks out its tongue across the river toward Kleinbasel. A copy hangs at the corner of the bridge on the Grossbasel side. In summer, look down and you may see locals floating downstream with colourful waterproof bags called Wickelfisch.

es.short: Este es el Puente Medio, en el lugar de uno de los cruces más antiguos del Rin, construido por primera vez hacia 1225. Une la Grossbasel, el casco antiguo sobre la colina, con la Kleinbasel, en la otra orilla.

en.short: Welcome to Basel Minster, the red sandstone cathedral with two slender towers that defines the city skyline. A church has stood on this hill for over a thousand years, and much of what you see was rebuilt after the great Basel earthquake of 1356.
en.long: The building mixes Romanesque and Gothic styles. On the west facade, look for Saint George fighting the dragon on one side and Saint Martin sharing his cloak on the other. Inside, you can visit the tomb of Erasmus of Rotterdam, the great humanist scholar, who died in Basel in 1536. Behind the church, the cloisters are quiet and atmospheric, and for a small fee you can climb one of the towers for a view across the Rhine to Germany and France. The church interior makes a good shelter if the weather turns.

es.short: Bienvenido a la catedral de Basilea, el templo de arenisca roja con dos torres esbeltas que define la silueta de la ciudad. Gran parte de lo que ves se reconstruyó tras el gran terremoto de 1356, y aquí está enterrado Erasmo de Róterdam.

en.short: This is the Pfalz, the terrace behind the Minster, high above the Rhine. It is one of the best viewpoints in the city.
en.long: From here you look across the river to Kleinbasel. On a clear day, you can see the hills of the Black Forest in Germany to the north-east. The Rhine bends sharply at Basel, and this is the point where it turns north toward Germany and the North Sea. Below you, watch for the small ferry crossing the river without an engine. That is our next kind of stop.

es.short: Esta es la Pfalz, la terraza detrás de la catedral, muy por encima del Rin. Es uno de los mejores miradores de la ciudad, con vistas hacia la Kleinbasel y, en días claros, la Selva Negra.

en.short: Down these steps is the Minster ferry, called Leu, meaning lion. Basel's four Rhine ferries have no engine: they are pushed across by the river's current alone.
en.long: Each ferry hangs from a steel cable stretched high above the river. By angling the rudder, the ferryman lets the current push the boat sideways across the Rhine. The ride takes just a few minutes and costs a few francs. It is a lovely, quiet way to reach Kleinbasel. The four ferries are called Wilde Maa, Leu, Vogel Gryff and Ueli, named after figures from Basel's traditions.

es.short: Bajando estas escaleras está el transbordador de la catedral, llamado Leu, el león. Los cuatro transbordadores del Rin en Basilea no tienen motor: la propia corriente del río los empuja de una orilla a otra.

en.short: This is the Spalentor, the most impressive of Basel's three surviving medieval city gates. It was built around 1400 as part of the outer city wall, which went up after the 1356 earthquake.
en.long: Look at the colourful glazed roof tiles and the gate's two crenellated side towers. On the outer face, statues show the Virgin Mary flanked by two prophets. You can still see the slot for the portcullis, the heavy wooden grate that was lowered to seal the city at night. The road through here led west toward Alsace, an important route for trade in wine and grain. Most of the old wall was demolished in the nineteenth century to make room for the growing city, but the gates were kept.

es.short: Esta es la Spalentor, la más impresionante de las tres puertas medievales que se conservan en Basilea. Se construyó hacia 1400 como parte de la muralla exterior, levantada tras el terremoto de 1356.

en.short: This Renaissance fountain on Spalenvorstadt is known as the Holbein Fountain. Its bagpiper figure and dancing peasants recall designs by the great artists of the time, including Hans Holbein the Younger, who worked in Basel.
en.long: Hans Holbein the Younger arrived in Basel as a young man around 1515. He painted portraits of the city's merchants and of Erasmus, designed house facades and stained glass, and later became court painter to Henry the Eighth in England. The figures on this fountain are inspired by prints of a peasant dance from the period. The original stonework is kept in a museum. This is a copy, but it gives a lively sense of the Renaissance city Holbein knew.

es.short: Esta fuente renacentista de la Spalenvorstadt se conoce como Fuente de Holbein. Su gaitero y sus campesinos bailando recuerdan diseños de los grandes artistas de la época, como Hans Holbein el Joven, que trabajó en Basilea.

en.short: This leafy square is Petersplatz, next to the old university buildings. The University of Basel, founded in 1460, is the oldest university in Switzerland.
en.long: Over the centuries, the university attracted figures such as the physician Paracelsus, the mathematicians of the Bernoulli family, and later the philosopher Friedrich Nietzsche, who taught classical philology here as a remarkably young professor. On Saturdays, the square often hosts a flea market, and every autumn it becomes part of the Herbstmesse, Basel's large autumn fair, which dates back to the fifteenth century. The Gothic church of Saint Peter stands on the eastern side.

es.short: Esta plaza arbolada es la Petersplatz, junto a los antiguos edificios de la universidad. La Universidad de Basilea, fundada en 1460, es la más antigua de Suiza.

en.short: In front of the theatre is the Tinguely Fountain, also called the Carnival Fountain. It was created in 1977 by the Swiss artist Jean Tinguely, and its ten black machines splash, spin and squirt water all day long.
en.long: The fountain stands where the stage of the old city theatre once was, and the machines are meant to be actors performing in a play that never ends. Tinguely built them from scrap metal and old machine parts, which is typical of his playful, noisy kinetic art. Watch for a moment and give each machine a name: there is a showman, a spinner and a water sprayer that seems to aim at passers-by. In very cold winters the spray freezes into wonderful ice sculptures. If you enjoy this, the Museum Tinguely on the Rhine has a whole collection of his machines.

es.short: Frente al teatro está la Fuente de Tinguely, también llamada Fuente del Carnaval. La creó en 1977 el artista suizo Jean Tinguely, y sus diez máquinas negras salpican, giran y lanzan agua todo el día.

en.short: This building is the Kunsthalle Basel, which has shown contemporary art since 1872. It does not have a permanent collection. Instead, it presents changing exhibitions, often by artists at the start of their international careers.
en.long: The Kunsthalle is run by the Basler Kunstverein, an art society founded by local citizens in the nineteenth century. Many artists who later became famous had early shows here. The building also houses an architecture museum and a popular restaurant with a garden terrace. Each June, Basel becomes the centre of the art world during Art Basel, one of the most important art fairs anywhere, and the whole city fills with exhibitions.

es.short: Este edificio es la Kunsthalle de Basilea, que muestra arte contemporáneo desde 1872. No tiene colección permanente: presenta exposiciones temporales, a menudo de artistas al inicio de su carrera internacional.

en.short: The tall Gothic church on Barfüsserplatz is the former Franciscan church, now home to the Historical Museum Basel. The Franciscans were nicknamed the barefoot friars, which gave the square its name.
en.long: Inside you will find treasures from Basel's past: medieval church treasures, tapestries, a famous Dance of Death painting fragment, and the original figures from the Fischmarkt fountain. The church itself survived the Reformation by being used as a warehouse. Barfüsserplatz outside is a busy hub, where trams meet, and it is a classic meeting point for locals. This museum is a great indoor option on a rainy day.

es.short: La alta iglesia gótica de la Barfüsserplatz es la antigua iglesia franciscana, hoy sede del Museo Histórico de Basilea. A los franciscanos los llamaban los frailes descalzos, y de ahí viene el nombre de la plaza.

en.short: This neo-Gothic church, completed in 1864, was paid for by the Basel philanthropist Christoph Merian and his wife Margaretha. It was one of the first major Protestant churches built in Switzerland after the Reformation.
en.long: Christoph Merian was one of the richest men of his time and left almost his entire fortune to the city. His foundation still supports social and cultural projects in Basel today. The couple are buried in the crypt of this church. Today it is run as an open city church, used for concerts, events and quiet reflection, and the café inside makes it a pleasant place to warm up.

es.short: Esta iglesia neogótica, terminada en 1864, la pagaron el filántropo Christoph Merian y su esposa Margaretha. Fue una de las primeras grandes iglesias protestantes construidas en Suiza después de la Reforma.

en.short: This is the Kunstmuseum Basel. Its collection began in 1661, when the city bought the Amerbach Cabinet, making it one of the oldest public art collections in the world.
en.long: The museum has the world's largest collection of works by the Holbein family, alongside masterpieces from the Renaissance to the present, including Picasso, van Gogh, Monet and many modern artists. In the courtyard of the main building, look for Auguste Rodin's sculpture The Burghers of Calais. Across the street is the newer extension, opened in 2016, with a grey brick facade and a frieze of light that can display text. If it starts raining, this is one of the best places in Basel to spend an hour.

es.short: Este es el Kunstmuseum de Basilea. Su colección comenzó en 1661, cuando la ciudad compró el Gabinete Amerbach, lo que lo convierte en una de las colecciones públicas de arte más antiguas del mundo.

en.short: This small square is named after Pablo Picasso, thanks to a remarkable story. In 1967, the people of Basel voted in a referendum to spend public money on two Picasso paintings for their museum.
en.long: The paintings had been on loan to the Kunstmuseum, and when the owner needed to sell them, Basel's citizens raised money in the streets, held a festival, and then approved public funding in a vote. Picasso was so moved that he invited the museum director to his home and donated several more works to the city. It is often told as one of the first times a population voted to buy art. Next time you visit the Kunstmuseum, look for these paintings.

es.short: Esta pequeña plaza lleva el nombre de Pablo Picasso gracias a una historia extraordinaria: en 1967, los habitantes de Basilea votaron en referéndum gastar dinero público en dos cuadros de Picasso para su museo, y el pintor, emocionado, regaló varias obras más a la ciudad.

en.short: On the elegant St. Alban-Vorstadt street is the Cartoonmuseum Basel, the only museum in Switzerland dedicated entirely to narrative drawing: comics, cartoons, caricature and graphic novels.
en.long: The museum shows changing exhibitions that treat comics as a serious art form, from political caricature to contemporary graphic novels. The building combines a historic house with a modern extension by the Basel architects Herzog and de Meuron, who are also famous for the Tate Modern in London and the Elbphilharmonie in Hamburg. Keep walking down this street if you have time: it leads to the St. Alban quarter with its medieval paper mill and quiet canals.

es.short: En la elegante calle St. Alban-Vorstadt está el Cartoonmuseum, el único museo de Suiza dedicado por completo al dibujo narrativo: cómics, caricaturas y novelas gráficas.

en.short: Towering over Aeschenplatz is the Hammering Man, a giant steel silhouette by the American artist Jonathan Borofsky. His motorised arm slowly swings a hammer, day after day.
en.long: Borofsky created a series of these figures for cities around the world, including Frankfurt, Seattle and Seoul. They are a tribute to working people and to the quiet, repetitive labour that keeps cities running. Here the figure stands in Basel's banking district, in front of a bank headquarters, which gives the work an extra layer of meaning. Public art like this is a reminder that you do not need a museum ticket to see great art in Basel.

es.short: Sobre la Aeschenplatz se alza el Hammering Man, una gigantesca silueta de acero del artista estadounidense Jonathan Borofsky. Su brazo motorizado balancea lentamente un martillo, día tras día.

en.short: This sunny promenade on the Kleinbasel bank is the Oberer Rheinweg. It is the city's living room in summer, with people sitting on the steps, eating ice cream and swimming in the Rhine.
en.long: Look across the water for the best view of the old town: the Minster towers, the Pfalz terrace and the houses rising steeply from the river. In summer, Basel locals jump into the Rhine upstream, stuff their clothes into a waterproof fish-shaped bag, and let the current carry them downstream. If you try it, only do so in summer, stay close to the bank and follow local safety advice. Several small buvettes, or kiosk bars, open along the river in warm months.

es.short: Este soleado paseo en la orilla de la Kleinbasel es el Oberer Rheinweg. En verano es el salón de la ciudad: gente sentada en los escalones, helados y baños en el Rin.

en.short: You are in the Rheingasse, one of the old lanes of Kleinbasel. This side of the river was once a separate town, and it still has a more relaxed, alternative feel, with bars, small shops and plenty of painted walls.
en.long: Kleinbasel belonged to the Bishop of Constance rather than Basel until the city bought it in 1392. For centuries the two sides teased each other, which is why the Lällekönig on the bridge sticks his tongue out toward Kleinbasel. Look closely at doorways, shutters and side walls as you wander through the lanes: you will find stickers, stencils, paste-ups and murals, many of them changing from month to month. Street art here is part of the neighbourhood's culture, so take photos, but please respect private property.

es.short: Estás en la Rheingasse, una de las viejas callejuelas de la Kleinbasel. Este lado del río fue una ciudad aparte y conserva un ambiente más relajado y alternativo, con bares, tiendas pequeñas y muchas paredes pintadas.

en.short: This large building on the riverbank is the Kaserne, a former military barracks from the 1860s. Today it is one of Basel's main cultural centres, with concerts, theatre and a lively courtyard.
en.long: The barracks were built on the site of a medieval monastery. After the army left, the complex was gradually taken over for culture and youth projects. Walk into the courtyard and around the side buildings to look for murals and graffiti. The area has long been a canvas for local artists, and the walls change regularly. In summer, the courtyard and the Rhine steps in front fill with people, and in August the square becomes the stage for the Basel Tattoo, a big military music festival.

es.short: Este gran edificio junto al río es la Kaserne, un antiguo cuartel militar de la década de 1860. Hoy es uno de los principales centros culturales de Basilea, con conciertos, teatro y un patio lleno de vida.

en.short: You are now in the Matthäus quarter, one of Basel's most diverse neighbourhoods. Keep your eyes open for large murals on building gables and colourful pieces in the side streets.
en.long: This working-class district grew quickly at the end of the nineteenth century, when Basel's chemical industry was booming. Today it is home to people from all over the world, with small grocery shops, cafés and corner bars. Many walls here have been painted in recent years, some as commissioned murals and others as independent works. Because street art changes often, treat this stop as a treasure hunt: see how many different artists' styles you can spot within one block.

es.short: Ahora estás en el barrio de Matthäus, uno de los más diversos de Basilea. Fíjate en los grandes murales de las fachadas y en las piezas de colores de las calles laterales.

en.short: Beneath the Dreirosen Bridge, the concrete walls along the river have become one of Basel's best-known spots for graffiti and urban art.
en.long: The current double-deck bridge, carrying cars below and trams and bicycles above, opened in 2004. The spaces under and around it have been used for graffiti, skateboarding and summer gatherings by the water. Many pieces here are large, colourful lettering styles, painted and repainted by crews over the years. From this point, the Rhine heads north toward the harbour and the border with France and Germany, which is only a couple of kilometres away.

es.short: Bajo el puente Dreirosen, los muros de hormigón junto al río se han convertido en uno de los lugares de grafiti y arte urbano más conocidos de Basilea.

en.short: Welcome to the Klybeck harbour area. Former industrial land along the Rhine has been taken over by temporary bars, gardens and artists, and the walls, containers and silos are covered in large-scale art.
en.long: Basel's Rhine ports are Switzerland's gateway to the sea: barges travel from here all the way to Rotterdam. As parts of the harbour fell out of use, the city allowed temporary projects on the old quays. Wooden structures, food stands and open-air stages sprang up, and the area became a magnet for street artists. This part of the city is changing fast, with new housing planned, so what you see today may look different next year.

es.short: Bienvenido a la zona portuaria de Klybeck. Antiguos terrenos industriales junto al Rin se han llenado de bares temporales, huertos y artistas, y los muros, contenedores y silos están cubiertos de arte a gran escala.

en.short: This pink sandstone building on the Rhine is the Museum Tinguely, designed by the Ticino architect Mario Botta and opened in 1996. It is dedicated to Jean Tinguely, the artist behind the fountain near the theatre.
en.long: Inside you can see dozens of his machine sculptures. Many of them are switched on at set times, or activated by a foot pedal, so they rattle, clank and whir as you watch. Tinguely, who grew up in Basel, was part of a generation of artists who wanted art to move, make noise and even destroy itself. Walk along the glass gallery called the Barca, facing the river, for a great view of the Rhine. The museum is an excellent choice if the weather is wet.

es.short: Este edificio de arenisca rosada junto al Rin es el Museo Tinguely, diseñado por el arquitecto Mario Botta e inaugurado en 1996. Está dedicado a Jean Tinguely, el autor de la fuente junto al teatro.

en.short: Under this great dome near the station is the Markthalle. It was built around 1929 as the city's wholesale market hall and today it is full of street-food stalls from around the world, a good stop for lunch or shelter from the rain.

es.short: Bajo esta gran cúpula cerca de la estación está la Markthalle. Se construyó hacia 1929 como mercado mayorista de la ciudad y hoy está llena de puestos de comida de todo el mundo: buena parada para comer o refugiarse de la lluvia.

en.short: Behind the old university buildings is the Botanical Garden of the University of Basel, one of the oldest botanical gardens in Switzerland. Its glasshouses make a warm, green shelter on a grey day.

es.short: Detrás de los antiguos edificios universitarios está el Jardín Botánico de la Universidad de Basilea, uno de los más antiguos de Suiza. Sus invernaderos son un refugio cálido y verde en un día gris.

en.short: This green riverside park, the Solitude, surrounds the Museum Tinguely. With its old trees and benches facing the Rhine, it is a calm spot to rest your feet.

es.short: Este parque verde junto al río, la Solitude, rodea el Museo Tinguely. Con sus árboles centenarios y bancos frente al Rin, es un lugar tranquilo para descansar los pies.

en.short: Between the station and the old town lies the Elisabethen park. Look for the Strasbourg Monument, a gift from the city of Strasbourg thanking Basel for helping its citizens during the war of 1870 to 1871.

es.short: Entre la estación y el casco antiguo está el parque Elisabethen. Busca el Monumento de Estrasburgo, un regalo de esa ciudad para agradecer a Basilea la ayuda a sus habitantes durante la guerra de 1870 a 1871.

en.short: This is the St. Alban Gate, another of Basel's three surviving medieval city gates. Surrounded by gardens and remains of the old wall, it once guarded the road east along the Rhine.

es.short: Esta es la puerta de San Alban, otra de las tres puertas medievales que se conservan en Basilea. Rodeada de jardines y restos de la antigua muralla, protegía el camino hacia el este a lo largo del Rin.

en.short: In this medieval mill on the St. Alban canal, the Basel Paper Mill museum shows how paper was made and books were printed by hand. Basel was a major printing centre in the age of Erasmus.

es.short: En este molino medieval junto al canal de San Alban, el museo del Molino de Papel muestra cómo se hacía el papel y se imprimían libros a mano. En la época de Erasmo, Basilea fue un gran centro de imprenta.

en.short: Rising above Kleinbasel are the Roche towers, designed by the Basel architects Herzog and de Meuron for the pharmaceutical company Roche. When they were completed, each in turn became the tallest building in Switzerland.

es.short: Sobre la Kleinbasel se alzan las torres Roche, diseñadas por los arquitectos basilienses Herzog y de Meuron para la farmacéutica Roche. Al terminarse, cada una fue a su vez el edificio más alto de Suiza.

en.short: The Wettstein Bridge links the Kunstmuseum side of the old town with Kleinbasel. It is named after Johann Rudolf Wettstein, the Basel mayor who in 1648 secured recognition of Swiss independence at the Peace of Westphalia.

es.short: El puente Wettstein une el lado del Kunstmuseum con la Kleinbasel. Lleva el nombre de Johann Rudolf Wettstein, el alcalde de Basilea que en 1648 logró el reconocimiento de la independencia suiza en la Paz de Westfalia.

en.short: This is Messeplatz, home of the Basel exhibition centre, where Art Basel takes place every June. Stand under the hall's huge round opening, the City Lounge, designed by Herzog and de Meuron, and look up.

es.short: Esta es la Messeplatz, sede del recinto ferial de Basilea, donde cada junio se celebra Art Basel. Ponte bajo la enorme abertura circular del edificio, la City Lounge, diseñada por Herzog y de Meuron, y mira hacia arriba.
